Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding CPO challenges and external laser source solutions:

## Core CPO Challenges

CPO introduces two primary engineering obstacles: thermal management, caused by placing the laser directly next to a high-value processor, and serviceability risk due to component failure, which may require replacing the entire processor package.

More specifically, laser sources require precise temperature control to maintain stable wavelength, output power, and reasonable lifetimes, and placing these temperature-sensitive components directly adjacent to high-power switch silicon creates a fundamental conflict.

## External Laser Source (ELS) Solution

The most effective architectural solution to CPO's core thermal and serviceability challenges is to decouple the laser with an External Laser Source (ELS). By relocating laser sources away from the switch ASIC to front-panel modules, CPO systems can maintain lasers at controlled temperatures while preserving hot-swap serviceability, with this approach standardized through External Laser Small Form-Factor Pluggable (ELSFP) specifications.

## Thermal Trade-offs

However, there are thermal trade-offs with ELS. High-output lasers generate more heat and degrade faster under thermal stress, with lasers and thermo-electric coolers accounting for ~70% of ELS power consumption. Additionally, the downside of the ELS is higher power consumption, as output power is lost at multiple stages due to connector losses, fiber coupling losses and modulator inefficiencies, requiring each laser to provide 24.5 dBm of optical power to compensate.

In March 2026 Nvidia announced $2B strategic investments in each of Lumentum and Coherent ($4B total) with multibillion-dollar purchase commitments and US fab capacity rights for lasers/optical components

The Optical Compute Interconnect (OCI) MSA launched March 12, 2026 at OFC with founding members AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and OpenAI — an open, protocol-agnostic WDM optical scale-up interface using UCIe on the chip side and parallel CWDM/DWDM fibers carrying NRZ, scaling toward 3.2 Tb/s; Meta also disclosed a 90-million-hour CPO reliability validation

OIF standards stack: Co-Packaging Framework IA (Feb 2022), 3.2T Co-Packaged Module IA (March 2023), ELSFP external-laser pluggable IA 01.0 (Aug 2023) and 02.0 (Jan 2025); ELSFP is the standardized answer to CPO laser serviceability ('TeraPoP' does not correspond to any identifiable standard — the relevant terms are TeraPHY (Ayar) and the OIF 3.2T CPO module)

LPO vs CPO status: LPO offers 30-50% lower power and ~15ns lower latency than DSP pluggables and is penetrating 800G short-reach links, with >8M 1.6T LPO ports forecast by 2027; at 1.6T (>30W) linear-retimed optics (LRO) is viewed as the more practical near-term option; pluggables are expected to dominate through 2027 with CPO reaching ~30% of 800G/1.6T port shipments in 2027; CPO photonics packaging market forecast ~$5B by 2031

Unsolved CPO problems: laser co-location (external laser sources required; lasers + thermoelectric coolers consume ~70% of ELS power; ~24.5 dBm launch power needed to cover connector/coupling/modulator losses), field serviceability (whole-package RMA risk, mitigated by detachable OSAs and front-panel ELSFP), thermal management next to kW-class ASICs (all announced CPO switches are liquid-cooled), and fiber-attach/packaging yield at volume
